mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which may stimulate economic growth and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not higher than baseline during low FEDFUNDS periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 5% signals labor market weakness, potentially leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX returns remain positive when UNRATE exceeds 5% in >40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When employment increases (PAYEMS) but unemployment remains high (UNRATE), it may indicate inefficiencies, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur in >50% of cases with these labor conditions.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production growth slowing in late-cycle expansion may predict negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur despite slowing INDPRO in >40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts (HOUST) may indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Negative returns occur when HOUST increases in >30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in retail sales (RSAFS) may signal weak demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur when RSAFS drops in >40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates alongside slowing GDP growth may predict negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur in >35% of cases with high FEDFUNDS and slowing GDP.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment with slowing employment growth may signal labor market tightness, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: Negative returns occur in >25% of cases with these labor conditions.
